data.title: HTTPS
data.tagline: Encrypt the connection between the browser and the website
data.description: HTTPS is HTTP protected by TLS. It helps prevent other parties on the network from reading or changing the traffic and lets the browser verify the server's certificate. It does not make unsafe application code or stolen passwords secure by itself.

use: Use browser features that require a secure context
Verify the domain presented by a server
avoid: Assume HTTPS prevents every kind of attack
Load insecure resources inside a secure page
Send secrets to the wrong server just because the connection is encrypted

lessonPractice.title: A login page uses https://, but the browser still warns because a script loads from http://. What should happen next?

options.label: Check certificate and domain, then load scripts, images, and other subresources through HTTPS
options.feedback: The page and its subresources need protected connections; mixed content may be warned about or blocked.

options.label: Keep the HTTP script and add a This site is trusted notice inside the page
options.feedback: Page copy cannot change transport security or stop the browser from blocking insecure resources.

options.label: Once a lock appears, label the company and every transaction as verified
options.feedback: HTTPS protects the connection to a domain; it does not verify the operator, content, or transaction.

data.agentPrompt: Audit login HTTPS: confirm the certificate covers the domain and is valid, redirect HTTP to HTTPS, and remove HTTP from scripts, images, and APIs. Recheck browser security and mixed-content errors without describing the lock as business verification.
